info.title: judt API
info.description:
The judt API creates and runs Apps. Each App has a sandbox, where you and agents edit and run its source, and a production deployment that serves it.

## Authentication

Send an API token as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header. A token belongs to one organization, and you create and revoke tokens in the dashboard. A token scoped to one App can reach only that App. Give that kind of token to an agent.

## Sandboxes

Creating an App reserves its address, but it doesn't start a sandbox or publish anything. There's no endpoint to start a sandbox. A request that needs the sandbox starts it first, so the first request after the sandbox goes idle takes longer. Files, Git, commands, commits, restores, previews, and deployments all need the sandbox.

The sandbox stops on its own when it's idle. If `sandbox_status` is `failed`, the most recent start failed, and the API retries it while the sandbox is needed.

## Retries

A request that changes something returns `200` with its result after the work is done. To retry a request safely, send an `Idempotency-Key` header. For 30 days, a retry with the same key and input returns the first request's result instead of repeating the work. If you don't send a key, the API generates one and returns it in the `Idempotency-Key` response header.

The API records file writes and deletes, commands, commits, and restores before it runs them. The response status tells you what to do next:

- `503` or `504`: the action is recorded but not finished. To get its result, retry with the same key. A new key would run the action again.
- `4xx` or `502`: the result is final. A retry with the same key returns the same response.

A `504 request_timeout` response says how far the work got and which event to check. The work continues, and a retry with the same key picks it up.

## Troubleshooting

To see what happened to an App's sandbox, deployments, and deletion, list its events with `GET /api/apps/{id}/events`. To see what the App's code did, including requests, output, exceptions, and failed builds, list its logs with `GET /api/apps/{id}/logs`.

## Time limits

Requests have the following time limits:

- Stopping the sandbox: 120 seconds.
- File writes, commits, and restores: 120 seconds.
- Commands: the command's `timeout_seconds`, up to 120 seconds, plus 60 seconds to stop it and save its result.
- Publishing, unpublishing, deleting an App, and changing production settings: 540 seconds, including any sandbox start.

If a file write, commit, restore, or command has to start the sandbox, it gets up to 120 more seconds.

## Errors

An error returns a JSON body in the form `{"error": {"code": "CODE", "message": "MESSAGE", "detail": "DETAIL", "request_id": "REQUEST_ID"}}`. The `code` value is stable, so check it rather than `message`. The `detail` value is optional.

name.description: The App's display name, up to 100 characters.

slug.description: The App's label under the App base domain. If another App has the slug, including a deleted App, or the slug is reserved, the request returns `409 slug_unavailable`. Reserved slugs: `staging`, `preview`, `api`, `www`, `local`. If you omit it, the API generates one, such as `teal-plucky-tatooine`.

template_id.description: The ID of the template to create the App from. To list templates, use `GET /api/templates`. Default: the Hello template. An unknown ID returns `404 template_not_found`.

production.description: Who can reach the published App. Default: public.

visibility.description:
Who can reach the published App:
- `public`: anyone.
- `password`: anyone with the App's password, for 60 minutes at a time.
- `private`: members of the App's organization, who sign in through judt.

Access tokens open password-protected and private Apps. The sandbox is always private to the organization.

password.description: The App's password, 8 to 128 characters. It's required when `visibility` is `password`, and it's accepted only then. Setting a new password signs out every browser that used the old one. Responses never include the password.

Idempotency-Retry-Window.description: How long you can retry with the same key, in seconds: 2592000 (30 days).

409.description:
- `idempotency_conflict`: the key was used with a different request.
- `idempotency_expired`: the key is too old to reuse.

get.description:
Returns the file as JSON. For a text file, `content` holds the text. For a binary file, `binary` is `true` and `content` is left out. To get the bytes, send `Accept: application/octet-stream`.

The `ETag` header holds the file's version. To skip an unchanged file, send its ETag in `If-None-Match`, and the request returns `304`.

To replace only a specific version, send its ETag in `If-Match`. To create the file only if it doesn't exist, send `If-None-Match: *`.
